transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I guess I'm just having some trouble following things lately. Like, down at the museum. People will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them... but then I realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. I just have to ask them to run it by me again. So... that's why I'm here.
When did you first notice this trouble following conversations? Was it something that started recently, or has this been going on for a while?

Well... it's been a while. I guess it really started causing noticeable trouble about two years and four months ago. Give or take. 

That's when I had to take over the museum liaison duties all by myself. My... well, a friend of mine passed away, so the job just fell to me. It's been since then.
Around the time your friend passed away and you took on the museum liaison duties, did you also notice changes in your mood, energy level, or how you were feeling overall?
No, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, it was a hard time, obviously. But as far as my mood or energy... I was fine, I guess. I didn't notice anything different there. Just what I mentioned before.
Besides having trouble following conversations, have you noticed any changes in your memory - like forgetting things you normally would remember, or having difficulty recalling recent events?
No, not really. I mean... I might misplace a pen or something, but... no big changes. My memory is fine. Just the... the listening part, I suppose.

When you're trying to listen to someone, does it feel like the words are unclear or hard to hear, or does it feel more like your mind is wandering away from what they're saying even though you can hear them fine?
I can hear them fine. It's just... my mind wanders, I guess. I just stop paying attention.
When you're in a quiet one-on-one conversation like we're having now, can you hear me clearly without any difficulty?
Yes. I can hear you fine.

You mentioned your mind wanders when people are talking to you at the museum. Does this happen just as easily when you're here talking with me one-on-one, or does it seem to happen more when there are multiple people around or when things are noisier?
I suppose it happens more when it's noisy. Or when there are a lot of people. Here, it's quiet, so... it's a bit easier to stay focused. But it still happens sometimes, I guess.

When you're in a quiet environment like right now, and you're really trying to concentrate on listening to someone, can you maintain your focus for a full conversation, or do you still find your attention drifting away even when there are no distractions around?
I don't know... I guess it still drifts sometimes. Even if it's quiet. I just... lose track of what's being said.
When you're reading something or watching a movie by yourself, can you maintain your focus on that, or do you find your attention drifting away there as well?

I suppose it happens then, too. Like, if I sit down with a gallery packet, or some notes... I start out fine. But after a few minutes, my eyes are just moving over the page. My mind wanders off. I usually have to go back and read the same part again.

When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting - something you're genuinely excited about - can you focus on that without your mind wandering, or does the attention problem happen even with things you care about?
I'm not really sure. I don't... I don't know if I've noticed it with things I like. Maybe. I just haven't paid that much attention to it.

When you're doing something that requires sustained attention - like having a conversation, reading, or watching something - do you find it hard to keep your mind on it most of the time, or only in certain situations?

I think... mostly. Like I said before, with reading... I'll sit with those gallery notes, and it's just a few minutes before my eyes are just scanning, not really taking it in. I have to start over. It's... just most of the time, I guess.

Besides having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety? Like, do you have trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you need to be moving around or doing something with your hands?
No, I don't think so. I'm not really... I don't feel restless like that. I can sit still just fine.

When you're working or doing something, do you find yourself interrupting others, blurting things out without thinking, or acting on impulse? Or do you make careless mistakes because you're rushing through things?
I don't... no, I don't think I do that. I'm not really one to interrupt people or blurt things out. And I don't think I rush through things... just the trouble focusing, like I said.

You mentioned you can sit still just fine. But when you're sitting - say, at your desk working or waiting somewhere - do your legs bounce, do you tap your fingers, or do you find yourself shifting around a lot without really thinking about it?
No, not really. I just... I just sit there. I don't really do any of that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent inattention symptoms (difficulty maintaining focus during conversations, reading, and sustained tasks) that have been present for approximately 2 years and 4 months. The inattention occurs across multiple contexts (conversations, reading, watching) and is most prominent but not exclusively limited to high-stimulation environments. Notably, the patient denies hyperactivity symptoms, impulsivity, and restlessness. While the symptom onset coincided with a significant psychosocial stressor (friend's death and increased job responsibilities), the inattention persists even in quiet, low-distraction environments, suggesting an underlying attention disorder rather than purely stress-related adjustment. F90.9 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, unspecified) is most appropriate given the predominant inattention presentation without significant hyperactivity-impulsivity features.
